text:
Maya: Quick heads up — after we bumped prefetch window on a few hosts I started seeing p99 tail spikes. Can we do a short sync on prefetch granularity vs late-join penalties?

Sam: Which hosts/tenants? quick numbers help. Is this isolated to streaming/chat flows or general?

Maya: Host host-42, tenant T-42 is the largest offender. Short dump: p50=18ms p95=45ms p99=230ms after prefetch_window changed from 200ms -> 500ms. Seems related to late small requests getting stuck behind a big in-flight aggregation. Trace + logs: gs://redwood-perf/prefetch/host-42/1748511111.log

Leo: @Maya cool, from the traces it looks like larger prefetch increases batch size (good throughput) but amplifies contention when a late tiny request arrives and we hold slot/headroom. Two knobs: 1) make prefetch speculative (send early dispatch for suspected-late-joins) or 2) allow a small-request fastpath that can preempt an in-flight aggregation. Each has tradeoffs: throughput vs latency SLOs. :thinking:

Anya: Another axis: surface an "urgency" hint in the API so tenant can declare very latency-sensitive calls. Scheduler could prioritize those into the fastpath. Requires SDK/API change though.

Maya: Also thinking about adaptive headroom per-window — instead of a fixed headroom we scale headroom down for tenants with low burstiness. That reduces wasted capacity inside a window.

Sam: I worry per-tenant heuristics create oscillation and added complexity. What about a global microqueue fastpath: tiny requests (<= 8 tokens) go into a bounded microqueue that bypasses prefetch aggregation; main aggregator keeps doing big windows. Simpler surface, no tenant-specific rules.

Leo: Sketch of microqueue behavior:
```
# pseudo-config
microqueue:
  max_tokens: 8
  global_capacity: 200_tokens
  fallback_to_agg: true
```
Microqueue dispatches immediately if occupancy < global_capacity and request.tokens <= max_tokens. Otherwise it falls back to main aggregator. Need to track KV-cache warmup: small fastpath requests still pay cold-kv cost if we can't piggyback on warm batches.

Maya: Right — and with larger prefetch windows the KV cache stays warmer for longer but at cost of holding allocation. We should track metric: effective_tokens_per_sec * infra_cost_delta so we know the real cost impact.

build-bot: Benchmark artifact uploaded: /artifacts/prefetch-exps/1748511111/results.json — microqueue proto reduces p99 for small requests by ~3.8x, throughput delta ~ -1.6%.

Anya: Good win. Proposed next steps: 1) prototype microqueue on single staging pool, 2) add optional API urgency header, 3) run mixed-tenant perf tests and measure cold-kv miss rate and eviction churn.

Sam: Add telemetry requirements: microqueue_hits_per_tenant, microqueue_drop_rate, eviction_rate_during_microqueue, kv_miss_rate, and a circuit-breaker metric that trips if microqueue starves main aggregator.

Maya: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the prototype plan + telemetry spec and link the artifacts. TL;DR: hybrid approach (bounded microqueue fastpath + adaptive headroom) looks preferable to just shrinking prefetch windows. @Leo can you kick off the staging run and paste logs here when ready?

Leo: On it. Starting the staging run now (run id r-stg-1748511111). Will post perf summary in ~30m.

Maya: Awesome, thanks.

Sam: If proto looks good we should run a small canary on a dedicated host pool before rolling cluster-wide.

Anya: Agreed. Also add a small doc note in the console about "request urgency" if we decide to expose the header — helps customers tune.

Maya: Yep. I'll track RFC + canary checklist.
